_what: Which arrivals belong together as one moment, read by src/moments.mjs (the code names no row, no app and no kind of file). A moment is the things that came in close together in time and/or subject (photos, screenshots, voice memos, camera clips, recordings, the same words sent to several AIs): they are handed to the person's AIs as ONE job instead of one job each. `kinds` says what an arrival or an asked record is (source_kind): the first row whose `when` holds names it, over the facts kind (arrival or asked), route, job_id, file (the first file's name, or the recording's audio file) and from_person. `rows` say how each source_kind joins, the first row whose `when` holds is the one used, over those facts plus source_kind and has_text. A row is { id, label, when, window_minutes, quiet_minutes, most_members, most_span_minutes, late_minutes, signals }: an item joins a moment of the same row when any listed signal holds and it was written within window_minutes of a member (near_in_time: of the nearest member's time; same_conversation: the same source_id; same_text_across_apps: the same words after normalising, sent through a different app or conversation; shared_words: shares shared_words.min_shared words of shared_words.min_length letters or more); a moment never spans more than most_span_minutes or holds more than most_members. A row with window_minutes 0 means do not wait: the item is handed off at once as it always was (a chat the person is waiting on). A row with quiet_minutes above 0 holds its arrivals back and hands the whole moment off once nothing joined it for quiet_minutes; a row with quiet_minutes 0 holds nothing back: the first item is handed off at once and a later one that says the same joins that handoff, so the same words sent to two AIs are one job. late_minutes is how long after a moment closed an item may still join it while nobody has taken its job. A screenshot is told by its route, or by its file name only when the person took it (from_person true). `same_text` says how long a message must be (min_characters and min_words) before sending it to several AIs counts as one pasted brief: a short go-ahead line meaning continue your own job is never merged. `gather` bounds gather_moment: most_arrivals and most_asked read per call, most_range_minutes of range, most_folds open jobs closed per call, and pointer_most ids listed per kind in a job's pointer. A kind with `hear_first` true is a sound or video whose words are not in the arrival: the moment's job lists each such file and tells the taker to hear every one before acting, and never claims to know what was said. Changing a number or adding a kind of file is a row, never code. Why it exists: on 2026-10-08 one person's voice memos, photos and camera clips taken around one place were each handed to an AI as a separate job (about 4,400 jobs were open) and the same sentence typed into two AIs was worked twice.

rows.label: Photos, screenshots, voice memos and camera clips taken close together are one moment
The same words sent to different AIs are one job

words.title: Moment, {from}-{until} UTC: {counts}
words.lead: These {n} things arrived close together and belong together: treat them as one moment, read all of them, and finish this one job once. Each member's own words follow, with where to read it whole.
words.hear_first: Hear first: these members are sound or video, and their words are NOT in this job. Before you act on anything, hear every one of these files (list_files / read_file, or transcribe it): {files}. Do not assume what was said in any of them.
words.read_transcripts: Already written down: these members come with a transcript file beside the recording. Read each one whole with read_file before you act: {files}. Check it against the recording if anything looks wrong; do not assume more than it says.
words.late_lead: More of the same moment arrived after the first were handed to you ({n} more):
words.pointer: Nothing is lost: every member is kept. Messages: {messages}. Files: {files}. Asked records: {asked}. Read any of them whole with read_message, read_file or read_record.
words.pointer_more: {shown} and {more} more (read them with gather_moment dry_run or read_record on the moment id)
words.clipped: (shortened: the rest is in the member above)
words.same_words_job: The same words also came to {route} ({message_id}); they are already in this job, so there is nothing more to do for it.
